text: The boat came in at first light. The water was gray and then it was blue and the fish were down deep where it was cold. He had not eaten since the morning before. He did not think about that. He thought about the line and the weight on it and the way the sun would come up hard over the breakwater. A man does not need much. He needs to do the thing well. The rest is talk.

They sat at the table in the cafe and did not talk for a while. The wine was cold. She looked at the glass and then at him and then out at the street where it had begun to rain. It was good to be dry. It was good to have the wine and the bread and the small plate of olives. He poured for her and then for himself. We could go tomorrow, he said. All right, she said. She did not say anything else. There was nothing else to say and they both knew it.

In the fall the war was always there but we did not go to it anymore. It was cold in the mountains and the leaves came down. We walked through the town in the dark and saw the lights of the cafes. The dead were buried and the living drank and slept and woke and drank again. You learned not to ask about the others. You learned to carry your own pack and keep your feet dry and say nothing you did not mean.

He fought well in the early rounds. He kept his hands up and moved and did not waste anything. In the sixth he was tired. The other man knew it and came on. He took the punches on his arms and waited. When the chance came he hit him once, hard, under the heart, and the man sat down. That was all of it. He did not raise his arms. He went to his corner and spat in the bucket and looked at nothing.

The old man kept bees on the hill above the river. The hives were white and the grass was burned brown by August. He worked slowly in the heat and did not wear the veil because the bees knew him. Honey is honest, he said. It is what it is and nothing more. The boy listened and did not understand it then. He understood it later, after the old man was gone and the hives stood empty and the river ran low in the dry months.
